tier_reason: Lowered B to C. Enricher e113 (2026-10-05, while enriching resvg) found that the resvg-py 0.5.0 baseline used by the pillow-lunasvg benchmark builds resvg 0.48.0 with opt-level 'z' (baseplate-admin/resvg-py Cargo.toml, size-optimised), so the 2.8x over resvg-py measures a handicapped resvg build, not resvg; the other baseline, cairosvg, parses SVG in Python. The run is independent of LunaSVG's author but its baselines do not represent the compared libraries, so first-party-grade evidence only.

corrections.caveats: Measured by the author of the pillow-lunasvg wrapper (independent of LunaSVG's author, but promoting his own wrapper; added to LunaSVG's README via PR #273, merged 2026-09-17). The resvg baseline is resvg-py 0.5.0, whose Cargo.toml (baseplate-admin/resvg-py) builds resvg 0.48.0 with opt-level 'z', a size-optimised profile, so the 2.8x over resvg-py does not measure resvg's release performance; cairosvg parses SVG in Python. The pipeline is timed through Python: about 89% of pillow-lunasvg's 1.00 ms is Pillow load plus PNG encode (render only 0.11 ms), and the three tools use different PNG encoders. On the resvg test corpus LunaSVG does less work (no filters, CSS transform property, transform-origin, mix-blend-mode, context-fill or SVG/WebP inside <image>; 59% loose fidelity match against resvg) and per-renderer medians cover different file subsets; filter tests are not timed. The machine was not idle during the run (min-of-3 used). Baselines are Python packages, not the category's C/C++ incumbents.
